title: Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases Worksheet: Successor Runway Days
content:
**Definition.** For a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case reclassified on a borrower's death, the successor runway days are:

- the calendar days from the current resolution deadline to the runway end date; or
- zero, when the current resolution deadline already falls on or after the runway end date.

The figure is a whole number of calendar days.

**How the dates are formed.**

- The runway end date is the runway start date plus the runway length.
- The runway length is the base runway length with every addition made and every deduction taken. The additions and deductions change only the runway length, never the runway start date.
- The runway starts on the date the accepted death notice was received. That notice is the death notice on the borrower's occupancy profile.
- The base runway length is 30 calendar days.
- Nothing is added to or taken off the runway length.
- The current resolution deadline is the one the case carries on the day the figure is worked out.
- The case's as-is appraised value is the appraised value recorded on the case.

## Worksheet lines

| Line | Entry |
|---|---|
| A | date the accepted death notice was received (runway start date) |
| B | runway length: 30 calendar days |
| C | runway end date: line A plus line B in calendar days |
| D | current resolution deadline |
| E | successor runway days: calendar days from D to C, or zero when D falls on or after C |

## Worked examples (all dates hypothetical)

1. Line A is 10 March, so line C is 9 April. Line D is 25 March. Line E is 15 calendar days.
2. Line A is 10 March, so line C is 9 April. Line D is 9 April. Line E is zero, because the deadline falls on the end date.
3. Line A is 10 March, so line C is 9 April. Line D is 2 May. Line E is zero, because the deadline falls after the end date.
